name: New York
summary: The largest city in the United States: five boroughs of dense neighbourhoods tied together by a 24-hour subway, home to Wall Street, Broadway, world-class museums and food from everywhere.

curated-2026-10.title: New York places and neighbourhoods written for Prospero Companion
curated-2026-10.note: Well-known public places, institutions and employers from general knowledge. Businesses open and close and rents move fast here: treat this as a snapshot for fiction. Rents are rounded estimates of typical 2025 asking ranges, not listings. Coordinates are approximate neighbourhood centres.

curated-climate-2026-10.title: Approximate monthly climate for New York (Central Park)
curated-climate-2026-10.note: Rounded values in line with NOAA 1991-2020 normals for Central Park; refresh with scripts/world when network access to NOAA is available.

neighborhoods.name: Financial District
neighborhoods.summary: Wall Street, the World Trade Center and City Hall at the southern tip of Manhattan, with ferries leaving from the Battery.

neighborhoods.name: SoHo
neighborhoods.summary: Cast-iron loft buildings and cobbled side streets packed with flagship shops and galleries.

neighborhoods.name: Lower East Side
neighborhoods.summary: Old tenement blocks of immigrant history, now mixing delis, galleries and late-night bars, next to Chinatown.

neighborhoods.name: East Village
neighborhoods.summary: Walk-up apartments, cheap eats, dive bars and NYU students around Tompkins Square Park and St. Marks Place.

neighborhoods.name: Greenwich Village
neighborhoods.summary: Crooked tree-lined streets of townhouses, jazz clubs and cafes around Washington Square and NYU, running west into the West Village.

neighborhoods.name: Chelsea
neighborhoods.summary: Art galleries, the High Line, Chelsea Market and big tech offices on the West Side between the Meatpacking District and Hudson Yards.

neighborhoods.name: Flatiron and Union Square
neighborhoods.summary: Startup offices and showrooms around the Flatiron Building, Madison Square Park and the Union Square Greenmarket.

neighborhoods.name: Kips Bay and Murray Hill
neighborhoods.summary: East Side blocks of mid-rise apartments beside the hospital row on First Avenue, popular with young professionals and medical staff.

neighborhoods.name: Midtown
neighborhoods.summary: The skyscraper core: Times Square, the Theater District, Rockefeller Center, Grand Central and Penn Station, busiest on weekdays.

neighborhoods.name: Hudson Yards
neighborhoods.summary: A new district of glass towers, offices and a mall built over the West Side rail yards.

neighborhoods.name: Upper West Side
neighborhoods.summary: Prewar apartment buildings and brownstones between Central Park and Riverside Park, with Lincoln Center and the Natural History Museum.

neighborhoods.name: Upper East Side
neighborhoods.summary: Museum Mile on Fifth Avenue, Park Avenue co-ops and busier rental blocks toward the East River, plus a cluster of major hospitals.

neighborhoods.name: Morningside Heights
neighborhoods.summary: The academic neighbourhood around Columbia University and the Cathedral of St. John the Divine.

neighborhoods.name: Harlem
neighborhoods.summary: Brownstone blocks with deep African American and Latino cultural history, centred on 125th Street and the Apollo.

neighborhoods.name: Williamsburg
neighborhoods.summary: Former warehouses turned waterfront towers, bars, music venues and restaurants one subway stop from Manhattan, with a large Hasidic community to the south.

neighborhoods.name: DUMBO
neighborhoods.summary: Cobbled streets of converted warehouses under the Manhattan and Brooklyn Bridges, beside Brooklyn Bridge Park.

neighborhoods.name: Downtown Brooklyn
neighborhoods.summary: Brooklyn's civic and office centre, now dense with rental towers, beside Fort Greene, Barclays Center and BAM.

neighborhoods.name: Park Slope
neighborhoods.summary: Brownstone streets of young families sloping down from Prospect Park.

neighborhoods.name: Bushwick
neighborhoods.summary: Warehouses covered in murals, artist lofts, late-night clubs and a long-standing Latino community.

neighborhoods.name: Coney Island
neighborhoods.summary: The seaside amusement district at the end of the subway lines, quiet in winter and packed on summer weekends.

neighborhoods.name: Astoria
neighborhoods.summary: A diverse, food-loving neighbourhood of Greek tavernas, beer gardens and two-family houses near the East River.

neighborhoods.name: Long Island City
neighborhoods.summary: Glass towers on the Queens waterfront with Manhattan skyline views, plus warehouses, film studios and MoMA PS1.

neighborhoods.name: Flushing
neighborhoods.summary: A busy Chinese and Korean commercial centre around Main Street, beside Flushing Meadows Corona Park with Citi Field and the US Open grounds.

neighborhoods.name: Concourse
neighborhoods.summary: Art Deco apartment houses along the Grand Concourse, a short walk from Yankee Stadium.

neighborhoods.name: Belmont (Arthur Avenue)
neighborhoods.summary: The Bronx's Little Italy of bakeries, butchers and red-sauce restaurants, between Fordham University and the Bronx Zoo.

transit.name: New York City Subway
transit.summary: The 24-hour MTA subway, with lettered and numbered lines across Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx.

transit.name: MTA New York City buses
transit.summary: Local, Select Bus Service and express routes in all five boroughs; slow in Manhattan traffic.

transit.name: NYC Ferry
transit.summary: East River and harbour ferry routes linking Wall Street, Midtown, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx and the Rockaways.

transit.name: Staten Island Ferry
transit.summary: Free 24-hour ferry from Whitehall Terminal to St. George, passing the Statue of Liberty.

transit.name: PATH
transit.summary: Port Authority trains from Lower Manhattan and Sixth Avenue to Hoboken, Jersey City and Newark.

transit.name: Long Island Rail Road
transit.summary: Commuter rail from Penn Station, Grand Central Madison and Atlantic Terminal through Queens to Long Island.

transit.name: Metro-North Railroad
transit.summary: Commuter rail from Grand Central through Harlem and the Bronx to Westchester and Connecticut.

transit.name: Citi Bike
transit.summary: Docked bike share, including e-bikes, across Manhattan and much of Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx.

places.name: Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island
places.summary: Ferries from Battery Park to Liberty Island and the Ellis Island immigration museum.

places.name: 9/11 Memorial & Museum
places.summary: Twin reflecting pools in the footprints of the towers, with an underground museum.

places.name: Staten Island Ferry ride
places.summary: A free harbour crossing with views of the skyline and the Statue of Liberty.

places.name: The Dead Rabbit
places.summary: Irish-style taproom and cocktail parlour on Water Street, a regular on world best-bar lists.

places.name: SoHo shopping streets
places.summary: Flagship stores and boutiques along Broadway, Prince and Spring Streets.

places.name: Balthazar
places.summary: Long-running Parisian-style brasserie on Spring Street with a bakery next door.

places.name: Katz's Delicatessen
places.summary: Cavernous deli on Houston Street serving hand-cut pastrami since the nineteenth century.

places.name: Russ & Daughters
places.summary: Family-run "appetizing" shop on Houston Street for bagels, lox and smoked fish since 1914.

places.name: Essex Market
places.summary: Public market hall with butchers, cheesemongers and lunch counters, now in a modern building on Delancey Street.

places.name: McSorley's Old Ale House
places.summary: Sawdust-floored saloon dating to the 1850s that serves only its own light or dark ale.

places.name: Veselka
places.summary: Ukrainian diner on Second Avenue known for pierogi and borscht, open from breakfast to late.

places.name: Veniero's Pasticceria
places.summary: Italian pastry shop and cafe on East 11th Street dating to the 1890s.

places.name: Washington Square Park
places.summary: The arch, the fountain, chess players, buskers and NYU students.

places.name: Joe's Pizza
places.summary: Classic New York slice counter on Carmine Street, open since 1975.

places.name: The Stonewall Inn
places.summary: Gay bar on Christopher Street where the 1969 uprising began, now part of a national monument.

places.name: Caffe Reggio
places.summary: Dim, art-filled MacDougal Street coffeehouse open since 1927.

places.name: Whitney Museum of American Art
places.summary: Modern and contemporary American art in a Renzo Piano building at the foot of the High Line.

places.name: The High Line
places.summary: Elevated park on an old freight rail line running from the Meatpacking District to Hudson Yards.

places.name: Chelsea Market
places.summary: Food hall in the old Nabisco factory, with tech offices upstairs.

places.name: Chelsea Piers
places.summary: Hudson River sports complex with a gym, golf range, ice rinks and climbing walls.

places.name: Union Square Greenmarket
places.summary: The city's best-known farmers' market, four days a week.

places.name: Madison Square Park
places.summary: Small park facing the Flatiron Building, with rotating public art and the original Shake Shack.

places.name: Strand Book Store
places.summary: Huge independent bookshop at Broadway and 12th Street, famous for "18 miles of books".

places.name: Times Square
places.summary: Neon billboards, crowds and costumed characters at the crossroads of the Theater District.

places.name: Broadway theatres
places.summary: Around forty large theatres in the blocks around Times Square staging musicals and plays eight times a week.

places.name: Rockefeller Center
places.summary: Art Deco complex with the Top of the Rock observation deck, a winter ice rink and the Christmas tree.

places.name: Empire State Building
places.summary: Art Deco skyscraper with open-air observation decks on the 86th floor.

places.name: Grand Central Terminal
places.summary: Beaux-Arts rail terminal with a celestial ceiling, a food hall and the Whispering Gallery.

places.name: Grand Central Oyster Bar
places.summary: Vaulted, tiled seafood restaurant beneath Grand Central, open since 1913.

places.name: Museum of Modern Art
places.summary: Major modern art collection on West 53rd Street, from Van Gogh's "The Starry Night" to contemporary design.

places.name: Madison Square Garden
places.summary: Arena above Penn Station, home of the Knicks and Rangers and a major concert venue.

places.name: Edge
places.summary: Glass-floored outdoor observation deck jutting from the 100th floor of 30 Hudson Yards.

places.name: Central Park
places.summary: The 843-acre park between the Upper West and Upper East Sides, with lakes, meadows, a reservoir loop and the Delacorte Theater.

places.name: American Museum of Natural History
places.summary: Dinosaur halls, the blue whale and the Hayden Planetarium on Central Park West.

places.name: Lincoln Center
places.summary: Performing arts campus for the Metropolitan Opera, New York Philharmonic, New York City Ballet and Juilliard.

places.name: Levain Bakery
places.summary: Basement bakery on West 74th Street known for enormous six-ounce cookies.

places.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
places.summary: One of the world's great art museums, on Fifth Avenue at the edge of Central Park, with a summer rooftop garden.

places.name: Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum
places.summary: Frank Lloyd Wright's spiralling museum of modern and contemporary art.

places.name: Bemelmans Bar
places.summary: Piano bar in the Carlyle Hotel with murals by the creator of "Madeline".

places.name: Cathedral of St. John the Divine
places.summary: Vast, still-unfinished Episcopal cathedral on Amsterdam Avenue.

places.name: Apollo Theater
places.summary: Historic 125th Street theatre famous for its Wednesday Amateur Night.

places.name: Sylvia's
places.summary: Soul food restaurant on Lenox Avenue since 1962, with a Sunday gospel brunch.

places.name: Smorgasburg Williamsburg
places.summary: Saturday outdoor food market on the waterfront with dozens of vendors and skyline views.

places.name: Peter Luger Steak House
places.summary: Old-school German-style steakhouse under the Williamsburg Bridge, open since 1887.

places.name: Devoción
places.summary: Skylit Colombian coffee roastery with a green wall.

places.name: Brooklyn Bridge walk
places.summary: The 1883 suspension bridge's elevated promenade from DUMBO to City Hall.

places.name: Brooklyn Bridge Park
places.summary: Piers turned into lawns, sports fields and Jane's Carousel along the Brooklyn waterfront.

places.name: Juliana's
places.summary: Coal-fired pizzeria at the foot of the Brooklyn Bridge.

places.name: Barclays Center
places.summary: Arena at Atlantic Avenue, home of the Brooklyn Nets and big concerts.

places.name: Junior's
places.summary: Diner on Flatbush Avenue Extension famous for its cheesecake since 1950.

places.name: Prospect Park
places.summary: Brooklyn's great park by the designers of Central Park, with the Long Meadow, a lake and Saturday Grand Army Plaza Greenmarket.

places.name: House of Yes
places.summary: Club and performance space with aerialists, costumed theme nights and dancing until late.

places.name: Roberta's
places.summary: Wood-fired pizza in a cinderblock building that helped put Bushwick on the food map.

places.name: Coney Island Beach and Boardwalk
places.summary: Wide public sand beach and wooden boardwalk with lifeguards in season.

places.name: Luna Park and the Cyclone
places.summary: Amusement park rides beside the 1927 Cyclone wooden roller coaster and the Wonder Wheel.

places.name: Nathan's Famous
places.summary: The original 1916 hot dog stand on Surf Avenue, site of the Fourth of July eating contest.

places.name: Museum of the Moving Image
places.summary: Film, television and video game museum with a cinema, beside Kaufman Astoria Studios.

places.name: Bohemian Hall & Beer Garden
places.summary: Czech beer hall with a big tree-shaded garden, open since 1910.

places.name: MoMA PS1
places.summary: Contemporary art in a former public school, with summer courtyard parties.

places.name: Flushing Meadows Corona Park
places.summary: Former World's Fair grounds with the Unisphere, the Queens Museum and lakes.

places.name: USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center
places.summary: Home of the US Open, with Arthur Ashe Stadium at its centre.

places.name: Citi Field
places.summary: The New York Mets' ballpark beside Flushing Meadows.

places.name: Yankee Stadium
places.summary: The Yankees' ballpark on 161st Street, with Monument Park beyond the outfield.

places.name: Arthur Avenue Retail Market
places.summary: Indoor Italian market from the 1940s with butchers, a cigar roller and sandwich counters.

places.name: Bronx Zoo
places.summary: One of the largest city zoos in the country, in Bronx Park beside Belmont.

colleges.name: The City College of New York (CUNY)
New York City College of Technology (CUNY)

employers.name: NYU Langone Health
employers.summary: Academic medical centre on First Avenue and one of the city's largest employers.

employers.name: The Mount Sinai Hospital
employers.summary: Flagship hospital and medical school on Fifth Avenue at 100th Street, facing Central Park.

employers.name: NewYork-Presbyterian/Weill Cornell Medical Center
employers.summary: Large teaching hospital on York Avenue.

employers.name: Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center
employers.summary: Cancer hospital and research institute on the East Side.

employers.name: JPMorgan Chase
employers.summary: The largest US bank, headquartered in a new tower at 270 Park Avenue.

employers.name: Goldman Sachs
employers.summary: Investment bank headquartered at 200 West Street by the Hudson.

employers.name: Bloomberg L.P.
employers.summary: Financial data and news company at 731 Lexington Avenue.

employers.name: Google New York
employers.summary: Google's largest office outside California, at 111 Eighth Avenue and nearby buildings on the West Side.

employers.name: Meta New York
employers.summary: Engineering and sales offices around Hudson Yards and the Farley Building.

employers.name: The New York Times
employers.summary: Newsroom and digital teams in the Times Building on Eighth Avenue.

employers.name: Condé Nast
employers.summary: Magazine publisher of Vogue and The New Yorker, based at One World Trade Center.

employers.name: Ralph Lauren
employers.summary: Fashion house with headquarters and design studios on Madison Avenue.

employers.name: Macy's Herald Square
employers.summary: The flagship department store on 34th Street, which also produces the Thanksgiving Day Parade.

employers.name: The Shubert Organization
employers.summary: Owner and operator of many Broadway theatres.

employers.name: Madison Square Garden Entertainment
employers.summary: Runs the Garden, Radio City Music Hall and the Rockettes' Christmas Spectacular.

employers.name: New York Marriott Marquis
employers.summary: Huge Times Square hotel with convention space and a revolving restaurant.

employers.name: Union Square Hospitality Group
employers.summary: Restaurant group behind Gramercy Tavern and The Modern.

employers.name: New York City Public Schools
employers.summary: The country's largest school district, run from the Tweed Courthouse.

employers.name: City of New York
employers.summary: City agencies around City Hall and the Municipal Building.

employers.name: Metropolitan Transportation Authority
employers.summary: Runs the subway, buses and commuter railroads from offices at 2 Broadway.

employers.name: Port Authority of New York and New Jersey
employers.summary: Runs the airports, bridges, tunnels, PATH and the region's container ports.

employers.name: Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom
employers.summary: Large law firm headquartered at One Manhattan West.

employers.name: Columbia University
employers.summary: Faculty, research and staff jobs on the Morningside campus.

employers.name: New York University
employers.summary: Faculty, research and staff jobs around Washington Square.

career_hubs.name: Midtown business district
career_hubs.summary: Corporate headquarters, law firms, Broadway, hotels and new towers from Hudson Yards to Park Avenue.

career_hubs.name: Financial District and Civic Center
career_hubs.summary: Banks, insurers, city government and the World Trade Center offices.

career_hubs.name: Silicon Alley
career_hubs.summary: Big tech offices on the West Side and startups around Flatiron and Union Square.

career_hubs.name: Garment District and fashion
career_hubs.summary: Showrooms, design studios and fabric shops in the West 30s, near FIT and Herald Square.

career_hubs.name: East Side hospital corridor
career_hubs.summary: Hospital rows along York and First Avenues, plus the Alexandria Center for Life Science.

career_hubs.name: Downtown Brooklyn and Long Island City
career_hubs.summary: Back offices, courts, colleges, film studios and warehouses just across the East River.

climate.summary: Humid subtropical: hot, humid summers with thunderstorms, pleasant springs and autumns, and cold winters with a few snowstorms most years.

months.note: Coldest month; snow and icy wind off the rivers.
Cold and grey; the snowiest month on average.
Changeable; early blossoms late in the month.
Mild and green; outdoor dining fills up.
Warm; beaches open Memorial Day weekend.
Hot and humid; many locals leave town.
Cool; leaves turn in the parks.

annual_events.name: New York Fashion Week
annual_events.summary: Runway shows and showroom presentations at venues around Manhattan each February and September.

annual_events.name: Tribeca Festival
annual_events.summary: Film festival with premieres and talks, centred on Tribeca in Lower Manhattan.

annual_events.name: NYC Pride March
annual_events.summary: The last Sunday in June, ending in the Village near the Stonewall Inn.

annual_events.name: Mermaid Parade
annual_events.summary: Costumed summer parade along the Coney Island boardwalk.

annual_events.name: Shakespeare in the Park
annual_events.summary: Free Public Theater productions at the Delacorte Theater in Central Park.

annual_events.name: SummerStage
annual_events.summary: Outdoor concerts in city parks, with its main stage in Central Park.

annual_events.name: US Open tennis
annual_events.summary: Two weeks of Grand Slam tennis around Labor Day at Flushing Meadows.

annual_events.name: West Indian American Day Carnival
annual_events.summary: Labor Day parade of Caribbean costumes and soca along Eastern Parkway in Brooklyn.

annual_events.name: Village Halloween Parade
annual_events.summary: Night-time costume parade up Sixth Avenue on October 31.

annual_events.name: New York City Marathon
annual_events.summary: Runners cross all five boroughs on the first Sunday of November and finish in Central Park.

annual_events.name: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade
annual_events.summary: Giant balloons travel from Central Park West to Herald Square on Thanksgiving morning.

annual_events.name: Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree
annual_events.summary: The tree is raised in November, lit in early December and stays up into January.

annual_events.name: New Year's Eve in Times Square
annual_events.summary: The ball drop at midnight, watched by huge crowds penned in from mid-afternoon.
